definition_en: to move or change, or a work period or a small change
core_image: 一群人交接班，工作位置从左移到右
scene: 她在医院上夜班。 She works the night shift at the hospital.
sceneCN: 这里 shift 是「班次」（第 3 个义项）；句意：她在医院上夜班。

derivatives.zh: 换挡杆
无进取心的
不断变化的

senses.title: To move
senses.definition: to move from one place or position to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一个地方或位置移到另一个
senses.example: He shifted the box to the left.
senses.exampleCN: 他把箱子移到左边。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的物理义项。

senses.title: To change
senses.definition: to change direction, opinion, or focus
senses.definitionCN: 改变方向、观点或焦点
senses.example: Public opinion shifted quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 公众舆论很快改变了。
senses.why: Physical movement becomes abstract change.
senses.whyCN: 物理移动引申为抽象改变。

senses.title: Work period
senses.definition: a period of work in a factory or hospital
senses.definitionCN: 工厂或医院里的一段工作时间
senses.example: She works the night shift at the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 她在医院上夜班。
senses.why: Workers take turns, so time is divided.
senses.whyCN: 工人轮换，时间因此被划分。

senses.title: Small change
senses.definition: a small but important change
senses.definitionCN: 微小但重要的变化
senses.example: There was a shift in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 风向发生了变化。
senses.why: The noun names the result of shifting.
senses.whyCN: 名词指转移带来的结果。

intro.en: Shift began as a word for arranging and dividing things.
intro.cn: shift 最初表示安排和分配事物。

items.en: Sciftan meant to arrange or divide.
items.cn: sciftan 意为安排或划分。

items.en: Skipta meant to exchange or share out.
items.cn: skipta 意为交换或分配。

items.en: Shiften covered changing position or clothes.
items.cn: shiften 涵盖换位置或换衣服。

items.en: Shift named a period of work.
items.cn: shift 开始指一段工作时间。

items.en: Shift grew into a noun for a small change.
items.cn: shift 发展为表示微小变化的名词。

note.en: Shift is compared with similar-looking words and with words for change and movement.
note.cn: 把 shift 与形近词以及表示改变和移动的词作比较。

entries.definition: a piece of clothing for the upper body
entries.definitionCN: 衬衫

entries.definition: a long narrow passage or rod
entries.definitionCN: 竖井；杆

entries.definition: to separate fine from coarse
entries.definitionCN: 筛分

entries.definition: to become or make different
entries.definitionCN: 改变

entries.definition: to go to another place
entries.definitionCN: 移动

entries.definition: to exchange one thing for another
entries.definitionCN: 转换

normalIntro.en: Shift is any move that changes place, time, or focus.
normalIntro.cn: shift 是改变位置、时间或焦点的任何移动。

normal.en: He shifted the box.
normal.cn: 他移动了箱子。

normal.en: The wind shifted.
normal.cn: 风向变了。

normal.en: She works the night shift.
normal.cn: 她上夜班。

normal.en: They shift gears on the hill.
normal.cn: 他们在山坡上换挡。

normal.en: The company shifted its focus.
normal.cn: 公司转移了重点。

abstract.en: A shift is a small move that changes everything.
abstract.cn: 转变是一个改变一切的小移动。

abstract.en: Night and day are two shifts of the same clock.
abstract.cn: 昼夜是同一座钟的两个班次。

abstract.en: To shift blame is to move a weight you should carry.
abstract.cn: 推卸责任就是搬走本该自己承担的重量。

examples.en: He shifted the box to the left.
examples.cn: 他把箱子移到左边。

examples.en: She works the night shift at the hospital.
examples.cn: 她在医院上夜班。

examples.en: There was a shift in the wind.
examples.cn: 风向发生了变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: shift 的核心画面是「换位」：换位置、换时间、换重点，都叫 shift。

root: 源自古英语 sciftan（安排、划分），核心义「分开并重新分配」。

sensesIntro.en: Shift means to move, to change, a work period, or a small change.
sensesIntro.cn: shift 意为转移、改变、班次或转变。

core.en: Dividing and moving things to new places.
core.cn: 把事物分开并移到新位置。

branches.en: A box moved to another spot.
branches.cn: 箱子移到另一个位置。

branches.en: Opinion turns a new way.
branches.cn: 舆论转向新的方向。

branches.en: A group takes its turn at work.
branches.cn: 一组人轮到上班。

branches.en: A small change in the wind.
branches.cn: 风的一点小变化。

branches.en: Movement of things and change of views share one word.
branches.cn: 事物的移动与观点的变化共用一个词。

intro.en: Shift forms a family of movement and work words.
intro.cn: shift 形成一个表示移动和工作的词族。

latinIntro.cn: shift 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 mutare（改变）只是语义对应词。

items.example: We need to shift the table.
She works two shifts a day.
The load shifted during the trip.
The shifting sand made walking hard.
items.exampleCN: 流动的沙子让行走变得困难。

items.meaning: a lever or person that shifts

items.example: He was called shiftless and lazy.
items.exampleCN: 他被称为无进取心又懒惰。

definition_zh: 准确的；精确的；精密的；忠实于事实的
definition_en: correct in every detail, exact in measurement, or faithful to the facts
core_image: 尺子贴紧木料边缘，刻度与墨线严丝合缝
scene: 木工把尺子压在板材上，反复核对后才下锯。 The carpenter made an accurate cut along the pencil line.
sceneCN: 这里 accurate 指下刀的位置与画线完全吻合（第 7 个义项：做工精细准确）；句意为木匠沿着铅笔线切了一刀，位置分毫不差。

pos.zh: 形容词：准确的；精确的；精密的；忠实于事实的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -acy 构成，义为「准确；精确度」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「准确地；精确地」
由否定前缀 in- 加本词构成，义为「不准确的；有错误的」
由 inaccurate 加后缀 -acy 构成，义为「不准确；错误之处」

senses.title: Correct and free from mistakes
senses.definition: containing no mistakes, especially of information, figures or details
senses.definitionCN: 尤指信息、数字或细节中没有错误
senses.example: Please check that the phone number on the form is accurate.
senses.exampleCN: 请核对一下表格上的电话号码是否准确。
senses.why: Latin cura is care: the word first means 'done with care', and careful checking is exactly what keeps a record free of mistakes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 cura 是「用心」：这个词最早是「用心做成」的意思，而核对时的用心正是让记录不出错的原因，于是「用心」就转成了「无误」。

senses.title: Exact in measurement
senses.definition: of an instrument, measurement or figure, able to give or show a true value within very small limits
senses.definitionCN: 指仪器、测量或数字能在很小的误差内给出或显示真实值
senses.example: A lab balance is far more accurate than a kitchen scale.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室天平比厨房秤精确得多。
senses.why: Care aimed at measuring means watching the smallest units; precision is care made visible on a scale.
senses.whyCN: 把「用心」用在测量上，就是盯住最小的单位；精密是「用心」在刻度上变得看得见的样子。

senses.title: True to the facts
senses.definition: of a description, report or memory, matching what actually happened
senses.definitionCN: 指描述、报道或记忆与实际发生的情况相符
senses.example: Her account of the accident was accurate in every detail.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那场事故的叙述在每个细节上都准确。
senses.why: A report is a reckoning of events, and accurate marks whether that reckoning matches the events themselves.
senses.whyCN: 报道是对事件的一次核算，accurate 标记的正是这次核算与事件本身是否对得上。

senses.title: Faithful to an original
senses.definition: of a copy, translation or model, keeping the features of the original without adding or losing anything
senses.definitionCN: 指复制品、译本或模型保留原件的特征，不增不减
senses.example: The museum sells accurate replicas of the bronze mirror.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆出售这面铜镜的精确复制品。
senses.why: Care can be turned towards an original: to reproduce it accurately is to follow it closely instead of inventing.
senses.whyCN: 「用心」也可以对着原件：准确地复制就是紧紧跟随原件，而不是自己另造。

senses.title: Well aimed or well judged
senses.definition: of a throw, shot or guess, landing exactly where it was meant to
senses.definitionCN: 指投掷、射击或猜测恰好落在预定的位置
senses.example: His pass was so accurate that the striker barely had to move.
senses.exampleCN: 他的传球极其精准，前锋几乎不用移动。
senses.why: The hand that is careful about aim is the same hand that is careful about numbers; both arrive at the intended point.
senses.whyCN: 对瞄准用心的手，与对数字用心的手是同一只手；两者都落在预定的那一点上。

senses.title: Correct in judgement
senses.definition: of a diagnosis, assessment or opinion, matching the true state of things
senses.definitionCN: 指诊断、评估或看法与真实情况相符
senses.example: The doctor's first diagnosis turned out to be accurate.
senses.exampleCN: 医生最初的诊断结果是准确的。
senses.why: Judgement is a reckoning of a situation; accuracy tests whether that reckoning holds.
senses.whyCN: 判断是对处境的一次核算；准确与否，就是检验这次核算站不站得住。

senses.title: Done with exact care
senses.definition: of work or a movement, carried out with close attention so that it fits the plan exactly
senses.definitionCN: 指活儿或动作在密切留意下完成，与预定的样子完全吻合
senses.example: The carpenter made an accurate cut along the pencil line.
senses.exampleCN: 木匠沿着铅笔线切了一刀，位置分毫不差。
senses.why: This is the word at its most physical: care shows in the fit between the tool and the line.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最具体的一面：「用心」体现在工具与那条线之间的严丝合缝上。

senses.title: Accurate to a stated limit
senses.definition: in the pattern accurate to, correct within a stated amount or decimal place
senses.definitionCN: 用于 accurate to 这一结构，表示误差不超过所说的量或小数位
senses.example: The thermometer is accurate to within half a degree.
senses.exampleCN: 这支温度计的误差在半度以内。
senses.why: Care has a reach that can be named; the phrase states how small the permitted error is.
senses.whyCN: 「用心」有一个可以被说出来的限度；这个结构说的就是允许误差小到什么程度。

intro.en: Accurate is a Latin past participle built on cura 'care'; its history is the shift from 'done carefully' to 'free from error'.
intro.cn: accurate 是建立在 cura「用心」之上的拉丁语过去分词；它的历史就是从「用心做成」走向「没有差错」。

items.en: Cura meant 'care, concern, attention', and it also lies behind cure and curious.
items.cn: cura 意为「关心、留意、用心」，cure 与 curious 也出自它。

items.en: Curare 'to take care of, attend to' is the verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: curare 意为「照管、用心对待」，是这一整个词族的动词来源。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus curare formed accurare, 'to do with care, prepare carefully'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 curare 构成 accurare，意为「用心去做、仔细准备」。

items.en: The past participle accuratus meant 'prepared with care, exact', and English took the adjective whole.
items.cn: 过去分词 accuratus 意为「精心准备的、精确的」，英语把整个形容词借了过来。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in English from the early seventeenth century, first for careful work and soon for exact figures and instruments.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十七世纪初进入英语，先指用心的活儿，很快又用于精确的数字与仪器。

note.en: The look-alike group is the word's own family of forms; the near-meaning group gathers close synonyms that stress closeness to truth or to a standard.
note.cn: 形近组就是这个词自己的词族形式；近义组收强调贴近真相或贴近标准的近义词。

entries.definition: The quality of being correct or exact.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「准确；精确度」，由本词加后缀 -acy 构成。

entries.definition: In a way that is correct and exact.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「准确地；精确地」，由本词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Not correct, containing mistakes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不准确的」，由否定前缀 in- 加本词构成。

entries.definition: A mistake or a lack of exactness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不准确；错误之处」，由 inaccurate 加后缀构成。

entries.definition: Marked by exactness in detail, often about measurement or wording.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「精确的、确切的」，多指测量或措辞上的细致精确。

entries.definition: Completely correct in every detail, with no allowance left over.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「精确的、丝毫不差的」，强调不留余量。

entries.definition: Right according to the facts or to a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「正确的」，强调符合事实或规则。

entries.definition: Showing great attention to small details in doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「一丝不苟的」，强调做事时对细节极为留意。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root cura 'care' and the everyday phrases the adjective appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 cura「用心」，以及这个词日常出现的搭配。

normal.en: Cura is care, so accurate work is literally work done with care.
normal.cn: cura 是「用心」，所以 accurate 的活儿字面上就是用心做出来的活儿。

normal.en: The same root gives cure: care is what both words are about.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 cure，两个词说的都是「用心照料」。

normal.en: Accurate figures are the ones you can check twice without finding a mistake.
normal.cn: accurate 的数字，就是你核对两遍也找不出错的那种。

normal.en: An accurate copy follows the original closely instead of adding anything.
normal.cn: accurate 的复制品紧贴原件，而不是自己添东西。

normal.en: Accurate to within half a degree tells you exactly how small the error may be.
normal.cn: 「accurate to within half a degree」把允许的误差说得明明白白。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler pressed to a board, the mark and the blade meeting with no gap.
abstract.cn: 想象尺子压在木板上，刻度与刀口之间没有缝隙。

abstract.en: Care is invisible; accuracy is what makes it visible on paper and on a dial.
abstract.cn: 用心是看不见的；准确就是让它在纸上和刻度盘上显形。

abstract.en: Things that are accurate can be checked by someone else, which is why the word suits facts and figures.
abstract.cn: 准确的东西别人也能核验，所以这个词特别适合事实与数字。

examples.en: Please check that the phone number on the form is accurate.
examples.cn: 请核对一下表格上的电话号码是否准确。

examples.en: A lab balance is far more accurate than a kitchen scale.
examples.cn: 实验室天平比厨房秤精确得多。

examples.en: The thermometer is accurate to within half a degree.
examples.cn: 这支温度计的误差在半度以内。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿Q瑞特」——阿Q拿尺子量了三遍，才把线画准：准确的、精确的。

root: 拉丁语 accuratus「精心准备的、精确的」，源自 accurare「用心去做」，由 ad-「朝向」+ curare「照管」构成；cura「用心、留意」是它的词根。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of accurate is care applied to some object: information, an instrument, a report, a copy, an aim, a diagnosis, a piece of work, or a stated margin of error.
sensesIntro.cn: accurate 的每个义项都是把「用心」用在某个对象上：信息、仪器、报道、复制品、瞄准、诊断、手上的活儿，或说出来的误差范围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler pressed against the edge of a board, the mark and the blade meeting exactly.
core.cn: 核心意象：尺子紧贴木板边缘，刻度与刀口正好对齐。

branches.en: FACTS AND REPORTS: care keeps information and descriptions matching what is true.
branches.cn: 事实与报道线：用心让信息与描述同真相保持一致。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: care becomes precision on an instrument, and the phrase accurate to names the margin of error.
branches.cn: 测量线：用心变成仪器上的精度，而 accurate to 结构把误差范围说出来。

branches.en: COPIES: care turned towards an original makes a faithful replica or translation.
branches.cn: 复制线：把用心对着原件，就得到忠实的复制品或译本。

branches.en: AIM AND JUDGEMENT: the hand and the mind both try to land on the right point.
branches.cn: 瞄准与判断线：手和心都试图落在正确的那一点上。

branches.en: WORKMANSHIP: the old physical sense, where care shows in how the tool meets the line.
branches.cn: 手艺线：最古老的具体的义，用心体现在工具与线如何相接。

intro.en: Accurate is a Latin participle pressed into English service; its endings still build the related nouns, adverbs and negatives.
intro.cn: accurate 是一个直接借入英语的拉丁语分词；它的词尾至今仍用来构成相关的名词、副词与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin cura, curare and accuratus are all recorded; only the deeper Indo-European root of cura is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cura、curare 与 accuratus 均有文献记录，只有 cura 更早的印欧词根属于重构。

items.example: It joins curare to form accurare.
items.exampleCN: 它与 curare 结合构成 accurare。

items.example: Cura is the care at the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: cura 是这个词核心的「用心」。

items.meaning: to take care of, attend to
items.example: Curare gives the verb behind the family.
items.exampleCN: curare 提供了这一词族背后的动词。
英语把 accuratus 借来作 accurate。

items.example: It carries the Latin participle into English.
items.exampleCN: 它把拉丁分词的形式带进英语。

definition_en: helpful for doing something, or able to serve a practical purpose
core_image: 一把随身小刀，开箱、削果、割绳样样都行
scene: 出门前母亲往包里塞了一把折刀，说路上总会有用得着的时候。 A small torch is really useful when the power fails.
sceneCN: 这里 useful 是「有用的」（第 1 个义项：能派上用场）；句意为停电时手电筒真的很有用。随身小刀件件都能用的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ly 构成副词，义为「有用地；有益地」
加 -ness 构成名词，义为「有用性；实用性」
去掉后缀后的基础词，义为「使用」
换成否定后缀 -less，义为「无用的」

senses.title: Helpful for a practical purpose
senses.definition: able to help someone do something or reach a result
senses.definitionCN: 能够帮助某人做成某件事或达到某个结果
senses.example: Her advice was useful, and I changed my plan.
senses.exampleCN: 她的建议很有用，我因此改了计划。
senses.why: The base verb names putting a thing to work; the suffix means full of, so the adjective marks what is full of workable use.
senses.whyCN: 基础动词指「让东西干活」，后缀意为「充满」；所以这个词就是「充满可用之处」的东西。

senses.title: Worth keeping for later needs
senses.definition: described of a thing worth having because it will serve a need later
senses.definitionCN: 形容某物值得留着，因为日后会用得上
senses.example: Keep the box; it may come in useful when we move.
senses.exampleCN: 把箱子留着吧，搬家时也许用得上。
senses.why: A thing that can be put to work at any moment is worth keeping, and that practical judgement gives this sense.
senses.whyCN: 随时能拿来干活的东西自然值得保留，这层「留着有用」的实用判断由此产生。

senses.title: Producing good effects on people
senses.definition: having a good effect on a person's knowledge, health, or work
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的知识、健康或工作产生良好作用
senses.example: The trip was useful for her spoken English.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟旅行对她的口语很有帮助。
senses.why: From tools the word extends to anything that leaves a person better off, such as a lesson or a habit.
senses.whyCN: 从器物再往外延伸，凡是让人变得更好的东西（如一堂课、一个习惯）也可以这样形容。

senses.title: Practical rather than beautiful
senses.definition: plain and practical in design rather than attractive
senses.definitionCN: 设计朴素实用而不追求好看
senses.example: The kitchen is small but useful, with everything within reach.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房不大却很实用，东西伸手就能够到。
senses.why: If a thing is judged by how well it works, plainness stops being a fault; this sense praises function over looks.
senses.whyCN: 既然以「好不好使」来评判，朴素就不算缺点；这层义项正是对功能的称赞。

intro.en: A native suffix, full of, laid over the borrowed verb use; the compound has been in English since the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: 一个本土后缀「充满」压在借入的动词 use 之上，这个复合词在中古英语时期就已存在。

items.en: The suffix -full meant full or complete and was freely added to nouns.
items.cn: 后缀 -full 意为「满的、完全的」，可自由加在名词之后。

items.en: The base goes back to uti and its participle usus, a using.
items.cn: 词基可溯至 uti 及其分词 usus，意为「使用」。

items.en: Us and user carried the verb into French and from there into English.
items.cn: us 与 user 把这个动词带进法语，再进入英语。

items.en: Use and the suffix -ful combine, and the final l is later dropped in spelling.
items.cn: use 与后缀 -ful 结合，后来拼写中省去了末尾的一个 l。

items.en: Useful settles into the standard form, and usefully and usefulness follow it.
items.cn: useful 固定为标准写法，usefully 与 usefulness 相继派生。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same use stem, and the near-meaning group sorts helpful words by strength.
note.cn: 形近组汇集同一 use 词干上的词，近义组按程度给「有帮助」一类的词排序。

entries.definition: to employ something for a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 使用；利用

entries.definition: having no use at all
entries.definitionCN: 无用的

entries.definition: the quality of being helpful
entries.definitionCN: 有用性

entries.definition: a person who uses something
entries.definitionCN: 使用者

entries.definition: giving practical help
entries.definitionCN: 有帮助的

entries.definition: useful in real situations
entries.definitionCN: 实用的

entries.definition: bringing a good effect
entries.definitionCN: 有益的

entries.definition: worth a great deal
entries.definitionCN: 有价值的

normalIntro.en: Read it as use plus full: full of use, therefore worth having at hand.
normalIntro.cn: 把它读成 use 加 full：充满用处，因此值得随手带着。

normal.en: Use plus -ful follows the same pattern as helpful and careful.
normal.cn: use 加 -ful 与 helpful、careful 走的是同一构词路子。

normal.en: Come in useful is the idiom for something that turns out handy later.
normal.cn: come in useful 是「后来派上用场」的惯用说法。

normal.en: The negative partner is useless, with -less instead of -ful.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 useless，用的是 -less 而不是 -ful。

normal.en: Usefulness and usefully show the noun and adverb built on the same stem.
normal.cn: usefulness 与 usefully 是同词干上的名词和副词。

normal.en: In British spelling the word has one l before the end.
normal.cn: 英式拼写里这个词中间只有一个 l。

abstract.en: Picture a pocket knife that opens boxes, peels fruit, and cuts string.
abstract.cn: 想象一把小折刀，开箱、削果、割绳样样能干。

abstract.en: Hear a stranger say that your note saved them an afternoon.
abstract.cn: 听陌生人说，你那页笔记替他们省了一个下午。

abstract.en: Feel a torch click on in a sudden blackout.
abstract.cn: 体会突然停电时手电筒咔哒一声亮起。

examples.en: The leaflet gives useful advice on saving water at home.
examples.cn: 这份传单给了在家节水的有用建议。

examples.en: A folding chair is useful when guests arrive suddenly.
examples.cn: 客人突然来时折叠椅就派得上用场。

examples.en: He found the grammar notes useful before the exam.
examples.cn: 考试前他觉得那些语法笔记很有用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优思否」——一样东西好不好用，先想一想它能不能替你省力。

root: 本土后缀 -ful（充满）加动词 use（源自拉丁语 uti / usus，经古法语 user），整体义为「充满用处」

sensesIntro.en: A core of full of use splits into practical help, keeping for later, good effects on people, and plain functional design.
sensesIntro.cn: 「充满用处」这个核心分成四路：实际帮助、留着备用、对人有益、朴素实用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pocket knife that answers many needs.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把能应付多种需要的小折刀。

branches.en: The task branch: it helps the job get done.
branches.cn: 任务分支：它帮着把事情办成。

branches.en: The keeping branch: it earns a place in the drawer.
branches.cn: 留存分支：它值得占住抽屉的一角。

branches.en: The person branch: someone is better off after it.
branches.cn: 对人的分支：有了它，人变得更好。

branches.en: The design branch: plain looks judged by how well it works.
branches.cn: 设计分支：朴素的外表以好不好使来评判。

branches.en: The judgement branch: worth is measured by future help.
branches.cn: 评判分支：价值按它日后能帮多少来衡量。

intro.en: A Germanic adjective suffix on a borrowed verb: what is full of use is useful.
intro.cn: 日耳曼语形容词后缀加在借入的动词上：充满用处的，就是有用的。

latinIntro.en: The stem comes from Latin uti, to use, whose participle usus gave the noun use.
latinIntro.cn: 词干来自拉丁语 uti（使用），其分词 usus 给出名词 use。

items.example: Use the small spoon for sugar.

items.exampleCN: usefully 说明有帮助地做事。
usefulness 命名这种性质本身。

items.example: A user is one who uses.
Usage records how something is used.
A misuse is a wrong use.

definition_zh: 一打；十二个；十来个；许多
definition_en: a group of twelve, or a roughly counted group of about that size
core_image: 蛋托里整整齐齐排满十二个格子
scene: 烘焙课开始前，老师把鸡蛋摆上台面，让学生数清楚每盘的数量。 We need a dozen eggs for the cake.
sceneCN: 这里 dozen 是「一打、十二个」（第 1 个义项）；句意是做这个蛋糕我们需要一打鸡蛋。

pos.zh: 限定词：一打的；十来个的

derivatives.zh: 由 dozen 加序数词尾 -th 构成，义为「第十二的」
dozen 的复数形式，义为「几十、许多」

senses.title: A group of twelve
senses.definition: a set of twelve things, especially eggs, bread rolls, or bottles
senses.definitionCN: 十二个一组的东西，尤指鸡蛋、面包或瓶子
senses.example: She bought a dozen eggs at the market.
senses.exampleCN: 她在市场上买了一打鸡蛋。
senses.why: Old French dozeine was built on douze, twelve, from Latin duodecim, so the word simply carries the number twelve inside it.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 dozeine 由 douze（十二）构成，而 douze 又来自拉丁语 duodecim，所以这个词本身就把「十二」装在里面。

senses.title: A large but approximate number
senses.definition: a large number of people or things, used loosely rather than exactly
senses.definitionCN: 大量的人或物，只是约略说法，并非精确计数
senses.example: Dozens of volunteers turned up before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 天还没亮就来了几十名志愿者。
senses.why: Because a dozen is a handy bundle, the plural dozens slid into the general sense of many.
senses.whyCN: 因为「一打」是一个顺手的打包单位，复数 dozens 就顺势滑向「许多」这个泛指。

senses.title: Used as a counting word before a noun
senses.definition: placed before a plural noun to count things in twelves
senses.definitionCN: 放在复数名词前，按十二个一组来计数
senses.example: The bakery sells two dozen rolls every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这家面包店每天早上卖出两打小面包。
senses.why: English keeps dozen unmarked after a number, so it works like a measuring word rather than an ordinary plural noun.
senses.whyCN: 英语里 dozen 跟在数词后不加 -s，因此它像量词一样使用，而不像普通可数名词。

intro.en: Dozen came through Old French from Latin duodecim, literally two and ten.
intro.cn: dozen 经古法语来自拉丁语 duodecim，字面是「二加十」。

items.en: The numeral two goes back to a root meaning two, and ten to a root meaning ten.
items.cn: 数词「二」可追溯到表示二的词根，「十」也有自己的古老词根。

items.en: Duodecim combined duo, two, and decem, ten, to name twelve.
items.cn: duodecim 把 duo（二）与 decem（十）合起来，表示十二。

items.en: Dozeine, from douze, named a set of twelve and was used for goods sold in bundles.
items.cn: dozeine 由 douze（十二）派生，指十二个一组，用于成捆出售的货物。

items.en: English borrowed the word as dozen and applied it first to bread and eggs; precise dating is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语借入作 dozen，最早多用于面包和鸡蛋；精确年代不确定。

items.en: The plural dozens took on the loose sense of many, and fixed phrases such as baker's dozen appeared.
items.cn: 复数 dozens 发展出「许多」的宽泛义，也出现了 baker's dozen 这类固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group consists of number words and derived forms; the near-meaning group names other quantities.
note.cn: 形近组是数词与派生形式；近义组收的是其他数量说法。

entries.definition: The plural, used for large approximate numbers.
entries.definitionCN: dozen 的复数，义为「几十、许多」，常与 of 连用。

entries.definition: The Latin numeral for twelve, literally two and ten.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语数词「十二」，字面为「二加十」，是 dozen 的远祖。

entries.definition: Twelfth, formed by adding the ordinal ending.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「第十二的」，由 dozen 加 -th 构成。

entries.definition: The exact number twelve, without a bundle sense.
entries.definitionCN: 数词「十二」，只表精确数目，不含「一捆」的意味。

entries.definition: A set of twenty, used in the same way as dozen for bundles.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「二十个」，与 dozen 一样是成组计数的单位。

entries.definition: A group made or handled together, without a fixed size.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一批」，数量不固定。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie dozen to the Latin two plus ten and to the daily picture of an egg tray.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 dozen 系在拉丁语「二加十」与日常的蛋托画面上。

normal.en: Duo plus decem is two plus ten, which is exactly twelve.
normal.cn: duo 加 decem 就是二加十，正好十二。

normal.en: Old French douze still means twelve today.
normal.cn: 古法语 douze 至今仍表示十二。

normal.en: After a number, dozen stays singular, as in two dozen eggs.
normal.cn: 跟在数词后，dozen 保持单数，如 two dozen eggs。

normal.en: Dozens of turns the exact bundle into a vague many.
normal.cn: dozens of 把这个精确的「一捆」变成模糊的「许多」。

normal.en: A baker's dozen is thirteen, a little extra to avoid short weight.
normal.cn: baker's dozen 是十三个，多给一个以免分量不足。

abstract.en: Picture an egg tray with every cup filled.
abstract.cn: 想象一个蛋托，每个格子都装满。

abstract.en: Picture twelve loaves lined up on a bakery counter.
abstract.cn: 想象面包店柜台上排好的十二个面包。

abstract.en: Picture a bundle tied with string, marked with the number twelve.
abstract.cn: 想象一捆用绳子扎好的东西，上面标着十二。

examples.en: He ordered a dozen roses for her birthday.
examples.cn: 他为她的生日订了一打玫瑰。

examples.en: Dozens of people waited outside the ticket office.
examples.cn: 几十个人在售票处外等候。

examples.en: The recipe calls for half a dozen apples.
examples.cn: 这个食谱需要六个苹果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「打枕」——一打枕头正好十二个，数着数着就记住了 dozen 是十二个一组。

root: 经古法语 dozeine 来自拉丁语 duodecim（十二），后者由 duo（二）与 decem（十）合成，字面即「二加十」。古法语 douze 至今仍指十二；英语借入后既指一打，也在复数中引申为「许多」。

sensesIntro.en: The exact bundle of twelve loosens into an approximate many, and then works as a counting word.
sensesIntro.cn: 精确的「十二个一捆」先松成模糊的「许多」，再充当计数量词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tray whose twelve cups are all filled.
core.cn: 核心意象：十二个格子全部装满的托盘。

branches.en: THE BUNDLE: the core sense is a set of exactly twelve goods.
branches.cn: 成组线：核心义是正好十二件货物组成的一组，即第一个义项。

branches.en: MANY: the plural loosens the exact number into a vague crowd.
branches.cn: 泛指线：复数把精确数字放松成模糊的一大群，即第二个义项。

branches.en: COUNTING: placed before a noun, it measures rather than names.
branches.cn: 计量线：放在名词前，它用来计量而不是命名，即第三个义项。

branches.en: A dozen eggs and two dozen rolls use the same bundle as a unit.
branches.cn: 一打鸡蛋与两打小面包，都把同一个「一捆」当单位。

branches.en: Dozens of people is the counting word stretched into a crowd.
branches.cn: dozens of people 就是把这个计量单位拉长成一大群人。

intro.en: Dozen is a borrowed whole word; its parts are Latin numerals rather than living English affixes.
intro.cn: dozen 是整体借来的词，它的构件是拉丁数词，而不是活的英语词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin duo and decem combine in duodecim, and Old French reshaped it into douze and dozeine.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 duo 与 decem 合成 duodecim，古法语又把它塑造成 douze 与 dozeine。

items.example: Duo is the first half of twelve.
Decem is the second half of twelve.
The Latin numeral is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁数词是直接来源。

items.example: French kept the numeral after the noun was borrowed.
items.exampleCN: 法语在名词借出后仍保留这个数词。
这个名词变成了英语的 dozen。

derivatives.zh: 由 dozen 加 -th 构成，义为「第十二的」

definition_zh: 看得见的；可见的；明显的；显而易见的
definition_en: able to be seen, or easy to notice and recognise
core_image: 远处有个小点，越走越清楚，最后能认出是一个人
scene: 雾散了一点，山顶的塔终于从灰白里显出来。 The far tower was not visible until the cloud lifted.
sceneCN: 这里 visible 是「看得见的」（第 1 个义项：能被眼睛看到）；句意为云散之前那座远处的塔看不见。由小点变成清晰人影的那段过程，就是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 看得见的；可见的；明显的

derivatives.zh: 加 -ly 构成，义为「明显地」
加 -ity 构成，义为「能见度；可见性」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「看不见的」
同根名词，义为「视力；愿景」

senses.title: Able to be seen by the eye
senses.definition: able to be seen, because light reaches it and then the eye
senses.definitionCN: 因有光到达并被眼睛接收而能被看到
senses.example: The far tower was not visible until the cloud lifted.
senses.exampleCN: 云散之前，那座远处的塔是看不见的。
senses.why: Latin videre, to see, gives the stem vis-, and -ible means able to be; visible is literally able to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 videre（看见）给出词干 vis-，-ible 表示「能被…的」，visible 字面上就是「能被看见的」。

senses.title: Easy to notice
senses.definition: clear enough to be noticed at once, though not necessarily seen by the eye
senses.definitionCN: 清楚到能被立即注意到，尽管不一定用眼去看
senses.example: There were visible signs of strain in his face.
senses.exampleCN: 他脸上有明显的疲惫迹象。
senses.why: What the eye can notice without effort becomes a general word for anything easy to detect.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛不费力就能注意到的东西，成了任何易被察觉之物的通用说法。

senses.title: Of light, within the range the eye can see
senses.definition: of radiation, having a wavelength the human eye responds to
senses.definitionCN: 指辐射的波长在人的眼睛能反应的范围内
senses.example: Visible light lies between the infrared and the ultraviolet.
senses.exampleCN: 可见光位于红外与紫外之间。
senses.why: Physics used the word for the narrow band of light that is literally able to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 物理学用这个词指那一段字面上能被看见的光。

senses.title: Open to public view
senses.titleCN: 公开可见的；可被查到的
senses.definition: of records or activity, able to be checked or seen by others
senses.definitionCN: 指记录或活动可被他人查看
senses.example: The accounts are visible to every member of the club.
senses.exampleCN: 账目对俱乐部每位成员都可见。
senses.why: A thing to be checked must first be seen, so records are described as visible to those allowed to look.
senses.whyCN: 要被核对的东西先得能被看见，于是记录被描述为对被允许查看者可见。

senses.title: Prominent in public life
senses.definition: noticed often by the public, as a role or a person
senses.definitionCN: 被公众频繁注意，如某个角色或人物
senses.example: She became a visible figure in the campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了这场运动中的显眼人物。
senses.why: The metaphor of being on view gives the modern sense of public prominence.
senses.whyCN: 「摆在人眼前」这个比喻给出了现代的公众显眼义。

intro.en: Visible is Latin visibilis, able to be seen, from videre, to see.
intro.cn: visible 即拉丁语 visibilis（能被看见的），来自 videre（看见）。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and its stem vis- spread into many later words.
items.cn: videre 意为看见，其词干 vis- 进入许多后来的词。

items.en: Visibilis added the ending -ibilis, meaning able to be, to the stem.
items.cn: visibilis 在词干上加 -ibilis（能被…的）。

items.en: Old French visible carried the word to English in the middle ages.
items.cn: 古法语 visible 在中世纪把这个词带进英语。

items.en: English used it first of things seen by the eye and soon of things merely plain.
items.cn: 英语先用它指眼睛所见之物，很快又指只是明白清楚的事。

items.en: Physics and administration then gave it the senses of visible light and visible records.
items.cn: 物理学与行政事务随后添上「可见光」与「可查阅记录」两义。

note.en: The first group holds the see-root family, the second the adjectives for clear and for hidden.
note.cn: 第一组收「看」词根族，第二组收表示清楚与隐藏的形容词。

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning in a way that can be seen.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「明显地」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being visible.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可见性、能见度」。

entries.definition: The opposite adjective, unable to be seen.
entries.definitionCN: 反义形容词，义为「看不见的」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to seeing.
entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词，义为「视觉的」。

entries.definition: Seeming true, or plainly seen.
entries.definitionCN: 看来如此，或明显可见。

entries.definition: So clear that it cannot be missed.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚到不会漏掉。

entries.definition: Clear from the evidence at hand.
entries.definitionCN: 由现有证据看得很清楚。

entries.definition: Kept out of sight, the opposite of visible.
entries.definitionCN: 藏起来不被看见，与 visible 相对。

normalIntro.en: Vis- (see) plus -ible (able to be): a short pattern shared with audible and sensible.
normalIntro.cn: vis-（看见）加 -ible（能被…的）：与 audible、sensible 同一套构造。

normal.en: Visible is vis- plus -ible, able to be seen.
normal.cn: visible 是 vis- 加 -ible，义为「能被看见的」。

normal.en: In- makes invisible; -ly makes visibly; -ity makes visibility.
normal.cn: in- 构成 invisible，-ly 构成 visibly，-ity 构成 visibility。

normal.en: Visible light is only a small band of the spectrum.
normal.cn: 可见光只是光谱中很窄的一段。

normal.en: Apparent and evident are close, but visible is about being seen first.
normal.cn: apparent 与 evident 相近，visible 更强调先能被看见。

normal.en: A visible sign is one you notice without being told.
normal.cn: visible sign 是不用别人说就能注意到的迹象。

abstract.en: See a tiny mark on the horizon become a tower.
abstract.cn: 想象地平线上一个小点变成一座塔。

abstract.en: Hear a fact stated so plainly that nobody can miss it.
abstract.cn: 听一件事说得太直白，谁都不会漏掉。

abstract.en: Picture a record book open on a table for anyone to read.
abstract.cn: 想象一本记录簿摊在桌上，谁都能读。

examples.en: The coast was visible from the top of the hill.
examples.cn: 从山顶能看见海岸。

examples.en: There were no visible marks on the wall.
examples.cn: 墙上没有可见的痕迹。

examples.en: The stain is barely visible in this light.
examples.cn: 在这种光线下那块污迹几乎看不见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为择伯」——为挑东西的伯父能一眼看见，因为东西摆在明处。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看见）→ visibilis（能被看见的）→ 古法语 visible → 英语 visible；同根词有 vision、visual、advise。

sensesIntro.en: To be seen by the eye spreads to being easy to notice, to light itself, to open records and to public prominence.
sensesIntro.cn: 「被眼睛看见」先扩到容易察觉、再到光本身、再到公开记录与公众显眼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a distant mark becoming a tower.
core.cn: 核心意象：远处的小点变成一座塔。

branches.en: The eye branch: the tower hidden by cloud.
branches.cn: 眼睛分支：被云遮住的塔。

definition_zh: 酸；酸味；酸性；酸液；尖刻的
definition_en: a chemical substance that reacts with a base, a sour taste or quality, or a sharp and bitter manner
core_image: 柠檬汁滴在舌尖，整张脸立刻缩紧
scene: 她切开一只青柠，汁水溅到指尖，顺手吮了一下。 The acid in the lemon made her wince.
sceneCN: 这里 acid 指柠檬里那种起反应的酸性物质（第 1 个义项：能与碱反应的化学物质）；句意为柠檬里的酸让她皱起了脸。

collocations.zh: 严峻的考验；决定性检验

senses.title: A chemical compound that reacts with a base
senses.definition: a substance that reacts with a base and turns litmus red, or a solution containing it
senses.definitionCN: 能与碱反应、使石蕊变红的物质，或含有这种物质的溶液
senses.example: Citric acid gives lemons their sharp taste.
senses.exampleCN: 柠檬酸使柠檬带上尖酸的滋味。
senses.why: Latin acidus simply meant sour; chemistry later fixed the word on the class of substances that taste sour and react with bases.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 acidus 本只表示「酸的」；化学后来把这个词固定到那一类尝起来发酸、又能与碱反应的物质上，起点仍是「酸」这一味觉。

senses.title: The sharp taste of lemon or vinegar
senses.definition: the sharp sour taste of lemon, vinegar or unripe fruit
senses.definitionCN: 柠檬、醋或未熟水果那种尖锐的酸味
senses.example: The clean acid of the grapefruit cuts through the rich sauce.
senses.exampleCN: 西柚清爽的酸味化解了浓重的酱汁。
senses.why: This is the sense the Latin adjective named first: a taste on the tongue, before any chemistry existed.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语形容词最早命名的义项：化学尚未出现之前，它就是舌头上的一种味道。

senses.title: The property of being acidic
senses.definition: the state of a soil, water or solution having a pH below seven
senses.definitionCN: 土壤、水或溶液酸碱度低于七的状态
senses.example: Farmers add lime to reduce the acid in the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 农民施石灰来降低土壤的酸性。
senses.why: From the taste, the word was extended to the measurable property that produces the taste.
senses.whyCN: 人们从「尝到的酸」进一步指向「造成这种酸的可测性质」，于是有了酸性。

senses.title: A strong corrosive liquid
senses.definition: a strong acid in liquid form, especially one that can burn skin or metal
senses.definitionCN: 液态的强酸，尤指能灼伤皮肤或腐蚀金属的那种
senses.example: The battery acid had eaten a hole in the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 电池酸液把地面蚀出了一个洞。
senses.why: The substance at its strongest becomes something you can pour, spill and be burned by, so the word names a dangerous liquid rather than a class.
senses.whyCN: 当这种物质浓到极处，就成了能倒、能洒、能灼人的东西；词义于是从「类别」落到一瓶危险的液体上。

senses.title: Bitter and cutting in manner
senses.definition: of a remark, tone or humour, sharp and unkind
senses.definitionCN: 指言语、语气或幽默尖锐而不留情面
senses.example: He made an acid comment about her new haircut.
senses.exampleCN: 他对她的新发型说了一句尖刻的话。
senses.why: A sour taste in the mouth is the body's own picture of a sour temper, so the taste word becomes a manner word.
senses.whyCN: 嘴里的酸是身体对坏脾气的现成比喻，于是味觉词自然变成了形容态度的词。

senses.title: The acid test: a decisive check
senses.definition: in the phrase acid test, a test that proves whether something really works or is genuine
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 the acid test，指能证明某物是否真的有效或真实的检验
senses.example: The cold winter was the acid test for the new heating system.
senses.exampleCN: 这个寒冬是对新供暖系统的严峻考验。
senses.why: Nitric acid was once used to tell real gold from false, and the phrase keeps that image of a test that settles the question.
senses.whyCN: 硝酸曾被用来分辨真金与假金，这个短语保留了「一试便见分晓」的画面。

senses.title: Rain made acidic by pollution
senses.definition: in acid rain, rain made acidic by gases released from burning fuel
senses.definitionCN: 用于 acid rain，指因燃烧燃料释放的气体而变酸的雨
senses.example: Acid rain has damaged forests across the region.
senses.exampleCN: 酸雨已经损害了这一带的森林。
senses.why: The adjective carries the chemical property into the weather, so a laboratory word ends up in the sky.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把这个化学性质带进了天气里，实验室里的词于是升到了天上。

senses.title: A sour boiled sweet
senses.definition: in British English, an acid drop: a small hard sweet with a sharp sour flavour
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中 acid drop 指一种小而硬、味道尖酸的糖果
senses.example: Grandma always kept a bag of acid drops in her handbag.
senses.exampleCN: 外婆的手提包里总放着一袋酸味硬糖。
senses.why: The taste that named the word comes back as the name of the sweet, because that sharp flavour is the whole point of the thing.
senses.whyCN: 当初给这个词命名的味道，回头成了糖果的名字，因为那股尖酸正是这种糖存在的理由。

intro.en: Acid goes back to a Latin adjective for sour, and every branch of meaning still starts from a taste on the tongue.
intro.cn: acid 上溯到一个表示「酸的」的拉丁语形容词，所有义项都从舌头上的味道出发。

items.en: The root *h₂eḱ- is generally reconstructed as 'sharp, pointed'; it is the source of Latin acer 'sharp' and acus 'needle'. Its link with sourness is old, but the exact path is not certain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语词根 *h₂eḱ- 表示「尖锐的」，是拉丁语 acer「尖锐的」与 acus「针」的来源；它与「酸」的联系很古老，但具体路径不确定。

items.en: The verb acere meant 'to be sour, be sharp', and the same family produced acetum 'vinegar'.
items.cn: 动词 acere 意为「发酸、带尖味」，同一词族还产生 acetum「醋」。

items.en: Acidus was the adjective for 'sour, tart, sharp', and it is the form English took.
items.cn: acidus 是表示「酸的、尖酸的」的形容词，英语借入的正是这个形式。

items.en: The neuter form acidum was used as a noun for a sour substance, and alchemists and early chemists applied it to acids as a class.
items.cn: 其中性形式 acidum 被当作名词，指带酸味的物质；炼金术士与早期化学家又用它指一整类酸。

items.en: English borrowed acid in the early seventeenth century as both adjective and noun; the chemical class sense settled soon after, and the figurative 'bitter' sense followed. Exact dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪初同时借入形容词与名词用法；化学类别义随后稳定下来，比喻的「尖刻」义再往后出现。确切年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group is the acid family in English; the near-meaning group gathers words for sourness and for eating away.
note.cn: 形近组是英语里的 acid 词族；近义组列出表示酸味与腐蚀的相关词。

entries.definition: Containing acid or having a pH below seven.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「酸性的、含酸的」，指酸碱度低于七。

entries.definition: The amount of acid in a substance, or a sour quality.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酸度、酸性」，也指尖酸的意味。

entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使变酸、酸化」。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酸化过程」，多用于土壤或海水。

entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「酸的」，是 acid 在技术义之外的日常说法。

entries.definition: Sharp and sour in a pleasant way, often of fruit or a small pie.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「酸而爽口的」，多形容水果或小馅饼。

entries.definition: Able to burn or eat away material; also used of bitterly cutting remarks.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「腐蚀性的」，也形容言语刻薄伤人。

entries.definition: Able to destroy metal or living tissue by chemical action.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「腐蚀性的」，指通过化学作用破坏金属或活体组织。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real Latin words and the everyday phrases acid appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的拉丁词，以及 acid 常出现的日常搭配展开。

normal.en: Acidus is Latin for sour, and acere is the verb 'to be sour'.
normal.cn: acidus 是拉丁语「酸的」，acere 是动词「发酸」。

normal.en: The same family gives vinegar its Latin name acetum.
normal.cn: 同一词族给了醋一个拉丁名字 acetum。

normal.en: Acid rain, acid test and acid reflux each carry a different edge of the same word.
normal.cn: acid rain、acid test、acid reflux 各自带着这个词不同的一面。

normal.en: An acid remark leaves the same taste in the ear that lemon leaves in the mouth.
normal.cn: 一句 acid remark 在耳朵里留下的味道，和柠檬在嘴里留下的一样。

normal.en: An acid drop is a sweet that tastes of the word itself.
normal.cn: acid drop 是一颗尝起来就像这个词的糖。

abstract.en: Picture one drop of lemon juice: the whole word starts there, then spreads into chemistry, weather, speech and sweets.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴柠檬汁：整个词从这里开始，然后蔓延到化学、天气、言语和糖果。

abstract.en: Sourness is a warning on the tongue, which is why the word also serves for words that sting.
abstract.cn: 酸是舌头上的警报，所以这个词也用来形容刺人的话。

abstract.en: The strongest acid is the one you can spill, so the word slides from taste to danger.
abstract.cn: 最强的酸是能洒出来的那种，于是词义从味道滑向危险。

examples.en: The acid in the lemon made her wince.
examples.cn: 柠檬里的酸让她皱起了脸。

examples.en: This soil is too acid for most vegetables.
examples.cn: 这块土对多数蔬菜来说酸性太强。

examples.en: He answered with an acid tone that ended the conversation.
examples.cn: 他用一种尖刻的语气回答，谈话就此结束。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱吸的」——小孩爱吸酸的柠檬，吸一口脸就皱起来：酸、酸味。

root: 拉丁语 acidus「酸的」来自动词 acere「发酸、带尖味」，同一词族有 acetum「醋」；更早一般认为与表示「尖锐」的印欧词根 *h₂eḱ- 有关，具体路径不确定。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses begin with one bodily fact: something tastes sharp. Chemistry names the substance, cooking names the taste, farming names the property, industry names the liquid, and speech borrows the sting.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都始于同一个身体事实：有东西尝起来是尖酸的。化学命名物质，烹饪命名味道，农事命名性质，工业命名液体，而言语借走了那股刺痛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of lemon juice on the tongue, and the face pulling tight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴柠檬汁落在舌尖，整张脸缩紧。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: chemistry turns the taste into a class of compounds and into a liquid strong enough to burn.
branches.cn: 物质线：化学把这种味道变成一类化合物，也变成能灼人的液体。

branches.en: THE TASTE AND ITS MEASURE: what the tongue feels becomes a property that can be tested in soil and water.
branches.cn: 味道与度量线：舌头感到的东西，变成了可在土壤和水中测量的性质。

branches.en: THE VOICE: a sour mouth becomes a sour temper, so the word describes cutting remarks.
branches.cn: 言语线：嘴里的酸变成脾气的酸，于是这个词用来形容刻薄的话。

branches.en: THE PROOF: acid once separated real gold from false, and the phrase still means a test that settles the matter.
branches.cn: 检验线：酸曾经用来分辨真假黄金，短语至今仍指一试便知分晓的检验。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY EDGE: the same word rides in the rain and sits in a bag of sour sweets.
branches.cn: 日常线：同一个词既藏在雨里，也躺在一袋酸糖里。

definition_en: an event that causes great damage or suffering, or a complete failure
core_image: 风暴过后，屋顶掀开一半，一把椅子挂在树枝上
scene: 水退到脚踝，墙上留着一条深色的线，家具全倒了。 The flood was the worst disaster in the town's history.

senses.title: An event of great harm
senses.definition: a sudden event such as a flood or fire that causes great damage
senses.definitionCN: 洪水、火灾之类突然造成巨大损失的事件
senses.example: The flood was the worst disaster in the town's history.
senses.exampleCN: 这场洪水是该镇历史上最严重的灾难。
senses.why: The world keeps its shape, but people lose theirs.
senses.whyCN: 世界还保持着形状，人的日子却散了。

senses.title: A complete failure
senses.definition: a plan or event that fails completely
senses.definitionCN: 彻底失败的计划或活动
senses.example: The concert was a disaster from the first note.
senses.exampleCN: 那场音乐会从第一个音起就是一场灾难。
senses.why: Nobody is hurt, and yet everything has fallen down.
senses.whyCN: 没有人受伤，可所有东西都塌了。

senses.title: A hopeless person
senses.definition: a person who is completely unable to do something well
senses.definitionCN: 完全做不好某件事的人
senses.example: He is a disaster in the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 他在厨房里简直一塌糊涂。
senses.why: The word lends its ruin to one clumsy pair of hands.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把自己的废墟，借给了一双笨手。

intro.en: Disaster came from Italian disastro, literally an ill star, and carried the old belief that stars shaped events.
intro.cn: disaster 来自意大利语 disastro，字面是「凶星」，带着星辰左右世事的旧观念。

items.en: Astrum meant a star, and astronomy read the sky for signs.
items.cn: astrum 指星辰，占星与天象之学都从天上找征兆。

items.en: Disastro joined dis-, bad, to astro, star.
items.cn: disastro 把表示「坏」的 dis- 与 astro（星）合在一起。

items.en: Desastre carried the word into French with the same sense.
items.cn: desastre 以同样的意思把词带进法语。

items.en: English disaster named a calamity blamed on an unlucky star.
items.cn: 英语 disaster 指归咎于凶星的灾祸。

items.en: The star faded, and the word kept only the ruin.
items.cn: 星辰的意味淡去，这个词只留下了废墟。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by a letter or two, while the meaning group names other large misfortunes.
note.cn: 形近组只差一两个字母，近义组则列出其他巨大的不幸。

entries.definition: a large dry area of land with little rain
entries.definitionCN: 雨水稀少的干旱大地

entries.definition: sweet food eaten at the end of a meal
entries.definitionCN: 餐后吃的甜食

entries.definition: causing great harm or failure
entries.definitionCN: 造成巨大损害或失败的

entries.definition: an event that causes great and sudden suffering
entries.definitionCN: 造成巨大而突然苦难的事件

entries.definition: a serious misfortune that brings deep distress
entries.definitionCN: 带来深切痛苦的严重不幸

entries.definition: a very sad event, especially one involving death
entries.definitionCN: 极悲惨的事件，尤指涉及死亡的

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a storm over a town to a kitchen ruined by one cook.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从笼罩小镇的风暴，走到被一个厨子弄乱的厨房。

normal.en: Dis- plus aster: a bad star was once blamed for every ruin.
normal.cn: dis- 加 aster：从前每场废墟都怪一颗凶星。

normal.en: A natural disaster arrives without asking.
normal.cn: 自然灾害从不先打招呼。

normal.en: A party can be a disaster and still be remembered fondly.
normal.cn: 一场聚会可能是灾难，却仍被人笑着记住。

normal.en: Disaster relief arrives after the water, not before.
normal.cn: 救灾总是在水来之后，而不是之前。

normal.en: One clumsy cook can turn a kitchen into a disaster area.
normal.cn: 一个笨厨子就能把厨房变成灾区。

abstract.en: Picture a roof half lifted off a house.
abstract.cn: 想象屋顶被掀开了一半。

abstract.en: Picture a chair hanging from a tree branch.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子挂在树枝上。

abstract.en: Picture a dark line left high on a wall by water.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上高处留着一条水退后的深色线。

examples.en: The earthquake was a disaster for the whole region.
examples.cn: 这场地震对整个地区是一场灾难。

examples.en: Poor planning turned the event into a disaster.
examples.cn: 糟糕的筹划把这场活动变成了灾难。

examples.en: Several disasters struck the coast that year.
examples.cn: 那一年海岸遭遇了好几次灾害。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disaster 记成「地砸死他」：地一塌，砸下来，就是一场灾难。

root: 来自意大利语 disastro，字面意思是「凶星」，由表示坏的 dis- 与 astro（星辰）组成。古人相信星辰决定祸福，于是把大祸归因于星象。这个词经法语进入英语后，星辰的意味逐渐淡去，只留下灾难与彻底失败的意思。

sensesIntro.en: From a flood that ruins a town, to an evening that ruins itself, to a cook who ruins dinner.
sensesIntro.cn: 从毁掉小镇的洪水，到自我毁掉的夜晚，再到毁掉晚饭的厨子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a house with its roof half gone and a chair in the tree.
core.cn: 核心意象：屋顶没了一半，椅子挂在树上。

branches.en: The first sense is the great event that harms many.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是伤害许多人的巨大事件。

branches.en: The second sense is a failure with no injury.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是没有伤人却彻底失败的事。

branches.en: The third sense lends that ruin to one hopeless person.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把这片废墟借给一个没救的人。

branches.en: A flood and a concert can both end in the same wreckage.
branches.cn: 洪水和音乐会，都可能收在同样的残局里。

branches.en: A failed evening and a failing cook share one word.
branches.cn: 失败的夜晚和失败的厨子，共用一个词。

intro.en: Disaster opens the star family: disaster, disastrous, and the astro- words.
intro.cn: disaster 打开了「星辰」一族：disaster、disastrous 以及 astro 系列。

latinIntro.en: Latin astrum, star, and Greek astron, star, give the astro- base in this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 astrum 与希腊语 astron 都指星辰，给出这一族的 astro 词基。

items.example: The fire was a disaster for the village.
items.exampleCN: 那场火对村子是一场灾难。

items.example: The decision had a disastrous effect.
items.exampleCN: 那个决定造成了灾难性的后果。

items.meaning: in a way that causes ruin
a small rocky body in space
items.example: An asteroid passed close to the earth.
items.exampleCN: 一颗小行星从地球附近掠过。

items.meaning: the study of stars and their supposed influence
the scientific study of stars and space
items.example: He teaches astronomy at the university.
The astronomer mapped the southern sky.
items.exampleCN: 那位天文学家绘制了南天星图。

items.meaning: a star-shaped mark used in printing
items.example: A small asterisk marks the note.
items.exampleCN: 一个小星号标出了注释。

definition_zh: 小队；班级；警察分队；小组
definition_en: a small group of people trained or organized to act together, such as soldiers, police officers, or team members
core_image: 一小队人肩并肩站成一列，随时一起行动
scene: 球场的更衣室里，队员们互相搭着肩。 The whole squad gathered before the match to hear the coach speak.
sceneCN: 这里 squad 是「运动队全队」（第 4 个义项：一起活动的整队成员）；句意为全队在赛前聚在一起听教练讲话。

pos.zh: 名词：小队；班；分队；全队成员

derivatives.zh: 与本词同源于意大利语 scuderia 相关词族，义为「中队（空军或骑兵）」
由本词加 room 构成，义为「警察分局的办公大厅」

senses.title: A small military unit
senses.definition: the smallest military unit, usually several soldiers acting under one leader
senses.definitionCN: 最小的军事单位，通常为若干士兵由一名班长带领
senses.example: A squad of ten soldiers guarded the bridge at night.
senses.exampleCN: 一支十人的小队夜间守卫那座桥。
senses.why: Soldiers stand and move as one block; the smallness is the point.
senses.whyCN: 士兵作为一个整体站立与行动，「小」正是要点。

senses.title: A police or emergency team
senses.definition: a small group of officers trained for one special kind of task
senses.definitionCN: 为某种专门任务训练的警务小组
senses.example: The drug squad raided the warehouse at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 缉毒小组在黎明突袭了那座仓库。
senses.why: Special dangers need a team that trains and moves together.
senses.whyCN: 特殊的危险需要一起训练、一起行动的小组。

senses.title: A school class or work group
senses.definition: a group of students or workers who do things together, often informally
senses.definitionCN: 一起行动的学生或工作者群体，常为非正式说法
senses.example: The whole squad stayed late to clean the classroom.
senses.exampleCN: 全班留下来很晚打扫教室。
senses.why: Informal speech borrows the military word for any close-working group.
senses.whyCN: 口语把军事词借来称呼任何紧密合作的群体。

senses.title: The members of a sports team
senses.definition: all the players available for a sports team, including reserves
senses.definitionCN: 一支运动队的全部可用队员，包括替补
senses.example: Two new players joined the squad this season.
senses.exampleCN: 本赛季有两名新队员加入阵容。
senses.why: The team as a pool of players is one block ready to move.
senses.whyCN: 作为球员集合的队伍是一整块随时可调动的力量。

senses.title: A squad assigned to punishment or duty
senses.titleCN: 执行惩罚或特殊任务的队伍
senses.definition: a group formed to carry out a specific harsh duty, such as a firing squad
senses.definitionCN: 为执行某项严酷任务而组的小队，如行刑队
senses.example: The firing squad stood in a straight line.
senses.exampleCN: 行刑队站成笔直的一排。
senses.why: The same small block of people is pointed at one grim task.
senses.whyCN: 同一小块人群被指向某项严酷任务。

senses.title: A group of friends or helpers
senses.definition: an informal group of friends who do things together
senses.definitionCN: 一起行动的朋友圈，非正式用法
senses.example: She brought her usual squad to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着老搭档们来参加聚会。
senses.why: Modern slang keeps only the togetherness, dropping the military tone.
senses.whyCN: 现代俚语只保留「同行者」之意，去掉军事色彩。

senses.title: To organize people into squads
senses.definition: to arrange people into small working groups
senses.definitionCN: 把人编排成小组
senses.example: The teacher squadded the students for the project.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把学生分成小组做项目。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb: making blocks out of many people.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作动词：把许多人切成一个个小块。

intro.en: Squad traveled from Latin through French military use, always meaning a small square of people formed for action.
intro.cn: squad 经由法语军事用法从拉丁语一路传来，始终指为行动而排成的方形小队。

items.en: A form related to exquadra is generally thought to mean "one's own square of troops", from quadra "square"; details are source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为其通俗拉丁语形式与 exquadra 相关，意为「自己的方形队列」，源自 quadra「方形」；细节来源不确定。

items.en: French escouade and Italian squadra meant a small formed group of soldiers.
items.cn: 法语 escouade 与意大利语 squadra 指编成的小队士兵。

items.en: The French army used escouade for the smallest drill unit.
items.cn: 十七世纪法军用 escouade 指最小的操练单位。

items.en: English took squad from French for the same small military block.
items.cn: 英语从法语借入 squad，指同样的小型军队建制。

items.en: The word widened to police units, sports rosters, and slang for a friend group.
items.cn: 词义扩展到警察分队、运动队名单以及指朋友圈的俚语。

note.en: Squad belongs to a family of group-words and shares its shape with the square family.
note.cn: squad 属于群体词族，且与 square 词族共享形状意象。

entries.definition: a shape with four equal sides, from the same Latin quadra
entries.definitionCN: 正方形；与 squad 同源于拉丁 quadra「方形」

entries.definition: a larger military unit of cavalry or aircraft
entries.definitionCN: 中队；同根的更大军事建制

entries.definition: to bend low with legs folded, or short and thick
entries.definitionCN: 蹲；矮胖的；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a group working or playing together
entries.definitionCN: 队伍；团队，最通用说法

entries.definition: an organized group within a larger force
entries.definitionCN: 单位；建制单位，较正式

entries.definition: the people who work on a ship, aircraft, or project
entries.definitionCN: 全体工作人员；船员

entries.definition: a military unit larger than a squad
entries.definitionCN: 排；比班大的军事单位

normalIntro.en: Five real hooks inside squad and its family.
normalIntro.cn: 五条 squad 词内真实记忆钩子。

normal.en: squad and square share the Latin root quadra: a squad is a square of people.
normal.cn: squad 与 square 同源于 quadra：一个班就是一「方」人。

normal.en: squadron is squad with -ron: a bigger flying or riding block.
normal.cn: squadron 加大后缀 -ron：更大的飞行或骑兵建制。

normal.en: Bomb squad, drug squad, firing squad: the word attaches to one special task.
normal.cn: 排爆小组、缉毒小组、行刑队：squad 总跟着一项专门任务。

normal.en: Sports news keeps squad for the full player list.
normal.cn: 体育新闻用 squad 指全队名单。

normal.en: Slang squad of friends: only the shoulder-to-shoulder part survives.
normal.cn: 俚语里 squad 指朋友团：只剩肩并肩的意思。

abstract.en: Picture four people standing shoulder to shoulder in a small square.
abstract.cn: 想象四人肩并肩站成一个小方阵。

abstract.en: Hear one whistle: the whole block moves at once, no one alone.
abstract.cn: 听一声哨响：整块队伍同时行动，无人落单。

abstract.en: See a coach pointing at a whiteboard list of names: the squad.
abstract.cn: 看教练指着白板上的名单：这就是全队。

examples.en: A rescue squad reached the mountain village before nightfall.
examples.cn: 救援小队在夜幕降临前抵达山村。

examples.en: The coach named the final squad for the tournament.
examples.cn: 教练公布了参赛的最终名单。

examples.en: Our project squad met every Friday afternoon.
examples.cn: 我们的项目小组每周五下午碰头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯夸德」——像「四夸」而蹲：四个人夸成一堆蹲成小方阵，一喊就走。

root: 一般认为 squad 经法语 escouade / 意大利语 squadra 上溯至通俗拉丁语 exquadra「方形队列」，源自 quadra「方形」；此路径为通常看法，细节来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: From the square block of soldiers, squad extends to police units, teams of players, work groups, and friends.
sensesIntro.cn: squad 从士兵的方形队列出发，扩展到警察分队、球员名单、工作小组与朋友圈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small square of people formed to act together
core.cn: 核心意象：为共同行动而排成的小方阵

branches.en: military blocks and the grim tasks they draw
branches.cn: 军事建制与其领受的严酷任务

branches.en: police units trained for one danger
branches.cn: 针对一种危险训练的警察小组

branches.en: civil groups borrowed for class, work, and friends
branches.cn: 借入班级、工作与朋友语境的民间群体

branches.en: the full roster of a sports team
branches.cn: 运动队的全部队员名单

branches.en: the act of dividing people into such blocks
branches.cn: 把人分成这种小块的动作

intro.en: Squad builds its family through the Latin square root quadra and size suffixes.
intro.cn: squad 的词族围绕拉丁「方形」词根 quadra 与大小后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root quadra, "a square", gives squad, square, and squadron their shared shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 quadra「方形」赋予 squad、square、squadron 共同的形状意象。

items.example: Latin quadra gives both square and squad their form image.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 quadra 给 square 与 squad 带来方形意象。

items.meaning: out of one's own; one's own square
items.example: Exquadra meant one's own formed square of troops.
items.exampleCN: exquadra 指自己编成的方阵。

items.example: A squadron of jets flew overhead.
items.exampleCN: 一个中队的战机从头顶飞过。

items.example: A quadrangle has four sides around a court.
items.exampleCN: 四合院式的庭院有四面环绕。

items.example: A small parade squad walked behind the band.
items.exampleCN: 一支小方队走在乐队后面。

items.example: The bomb squad closed the street for hours.
items.exampleCN: 排爆小组封锁那条街数小时。

items.meaning: the group assigned to an execution detail
items.example: The term firing squad dates from military law.
items.exampleCN: firing squad 一词源自军法。

items.example: The cheer squad practiced on the field.

derivatives.zh: 由本词加大后缀构成，义为「中队」
由本词加 room 构成，义为「警局办公大厅」

definition_en: the person in charge of a ship, aircraft, team, or group of soldiers
core_image: 站在船头第一个发号施令的人
scene: 船长下令收起船帆。 The captain ordered the crew to lower the sails.
sceneCN: 这里 captain 是「船长」（第 1 个义项：负责指挥一艘船的人）；句意是船长下令收起船帆。

derivatives.zh: captain 加 -cy 构成，义为「船长或队长的职位」
captain 加 -ship 构成，义为「领导职位与能力」
captain 加 -less 构成，义为「没有船长的、无人指挥的」

senses.title: The person in charge of a ship
senses.definition: the person who commands a ship or an aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 指挥一艘船或一架飞机的人
senses.example: The captain steered the ship into the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 船长把船开进港。
senses.why: Latin caput, head, gave capitaneus, chief, and the chief of a ship was its captain.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 caput（头）派生出 capitaneus（为首者），一艘船上的为首者就是船长。

senses.title: The leader of a team
senses.definition: the leader of a sports team or other group
senses.definitionCN: 运动队或其他团体的领导者
senses.example: She was made captain of the basketball team.
senses.exampleCN: 她被任命为篮球队队长。
senses.why: The image of the chief on a ship transferred easily to any group that needs a head.
senses.whyCN: 「船上的为首者」这一形象很容易转移到任何需要领头人的团体上。

senses.title: A rank of officer
senses.definition: a middle-ranking officer in an army or air force
senses.definitionCN: 陆军或空军中的中级军官军衔
senses.example: He was promoted to captain after five years.
senses.exampleCN: 五年后他被提升为上尉。
senses.why: Military ranks also name the person at the head of a company of soldiers.
senses.whyCN: 军衔同样取自「一队士兵之首」的意思。

intro.en: Captain comes from the same head word as capital: it names the head of a ship, team, or company of soldiers.
intro.cn: captain 与 capital 同出「头」这个词：它指船、队伍或连队之首。

items.en: caput meant head, the source of the root capit-.
items.cn: caput 意为「头」，是词根 capit- 的来源。

items.en: capitaneus meant chief or leading, formed from caput.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 capitaneus 意为「为首的、首要的」，由 caput 构成。

items.en: capitaine named a military leader or the commander of a ship.
items.cn: 古法语 capitaine 指军事首领或船只指挥官。

items.en: English borrowed it as captain for commanders on land and at sea.
items.cn: 英语借入为 captain，陆上与海上的指挥官都用它。

items.en: The word spread to sports teams and to a fixed military rank.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到运动队，并固定为一个军衔。

note.en: Captain belongs to the Latin head family, and it sits beside other words for leaders.
note.cn: captain 属于拉丁语「头」词族，同时也和别的「领导者」词相邻。

entries.definition: the position or period of being a captain
entries.definitionCN: 船长或队长的职位与任期，由 captain 加 -cy 构成。

entries.definition: chief, or the main city, money, or letter
entries.definitionCN: 首要的；首都；资本；大写字母，与 captain 同出 caput。

entries.definition: the leader of a group or organization
entries.definitionCN: 团体或组织的首领，同样源自拉丁语 caput。

entries.definition: the officer in charge of a military group
entries.definitionCN: 指挥一支军队的军官，与「上尉」义近。

entries.definition: the person who leads a group
entries.definitionCN: 带领一个团体的人，对应「队长」义。

entries.definition: an informal word for the captain of a boat or team
entries.definitionCN: 船长或队长的口语说法。

normalIntro.en: The head root is the key: a captain is the head of a ship, a team, or a company of soldiers.
normalIntro.cn: 关键是「头」这个词根：captain 就是船、队伍或连队的头。

normal.en: captain and capital share the Latin root caput, head.
normal.cn: captain 与 capital 共享拉丁词根 caput（头）。

normal.en: The captain is the head of the ship, which is why the word first meant ship commander.
normal.cn: 船长是船上的头，所以这个词最早指船只指挥官。

normal.en: The same head idea moved to sports, giving team captain.
normal.cn: 同样的「头」的想法移到运动上，就有了 team captain。

normal.en: In the army, a captain is the head of a company of soldiers.
normal.cn: 在军队里，上尉是一个连的头。

normal.en: As a verb, captain means to act as the head of a team.
normal.cn: 作动词时，captain 指担任队伍的头。

abstract.en: Picture a figure standing at the bow, the whole crew watching for a signal.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在船头，全体船员都等着他发信号。

abstract.en: Picture a captain's armband passed from one player to another.
abstract.cn: 想象队长袖标从一名球员传到另一名球员手上。

abstract.en: Picture a line of soldiers turning as one when the leading voice speaks.
abstract.cn: 想象一队士兵在领头人开口时齐刷刷转身。

examples.en: The captain ordered the crew to lower the sails.
examples.cn: 船长下令收起船帆。

examples.en: She was made captain of the basketball team.
examples.cn: 她被任命为篮球队队长。

examples.en: He captained the side for three seasons.
examples.cn: 他带领这支球队打了三个赛季。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开普顿」——开船的人站在最前面，就是船长。

root: 拉丁语 caput（头）→ 晚期拉丁语 capitaneus（为首者）→ 古法语 capitaine → 英语 captain。

sensesIntro.en: One role, several settings: the head of a ship, a team, or a company of soldiers.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个角色，几种场合：船上的头、队伍的头、连队的头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the person standing at the front, giving orders that others follow.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在最前面、发号施令而众人跟随的人。

branches.en: The maritime sense: the commander of a ship or aircraft.
branches.cn: 航海义：船或飞机的指挥官。

branches.en: The sporting sense: the player who leads the team.
branches.cn: 体育义：带领球队的那名球员。

branches.en: The military sense: an officer rank above lieutenant.
branches.cn: 军衔义：高于中尉的军官等级。

branches.en: All senses name a head who is responsible for the group.
branches.cn: 所有义项都指对团体负责的那个「头」。

branches.en: The verb captain generalizes the role to any team or side.
branches.cn: 动词 captain 把这个角色推广到任何队伍。

intro.en: Captain is formed on the root capit-, head, with the agent ending -ain.
intro.cn: captain 建立在词根 capit-（头）上，加上表示人的词尾 -ain。

latinIntro.en: Latin caput and capitaneus explain both captain and its relatives capital and chief.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caput 与 capitaneus 同时解释了 captain 及其亲属词 capital、chief。

items.meaning: the head of a ship, team, or company
items.example: The captain spoke to the passengers.

items.meaning: more than one captain, or he leads a team
items.meaningCN: captain 的复数，或动词第三人称单数
items.example: Both captains agreed to the rules.
items.exampleCN: 两位队长都同意了规则。

items.example: He captained the club for a decade.
items.exampleCN: 他担任这家俱乐部的队长十年。

items.meaning: the act of leading a team
items.example: She is captaining the side this season.
He took over the captaincy in May.

items.meaning: the role and skill of a captain
items.exampleCN: 她的领导让船员稳定下来。

items.example: Caput is the root of the family.

items.meaning: a leader or the most important person
items.meaningCN: 首领；最重要的人，与 captain 同根

definition_zh: 主管；高管；行政的；执行的；高档的
definition_en: a senior manager, the branch that carries out decisions, or goods made for top staff
core_image: 顶层那间有最终决定权的办公室
scene: 董事会任命了一位新主管负责日常运营。 The board appointed a new executive to run daily operations.
sceneCN: 这里 executive 是「主管、高管」（第 1 个义项）；句意：董事会任命了一位新主管负责日常运营。

derivatives.zh: 执行；处决
执行；实施
遗嘱执行人
以行政方式

senses.title: Top manager
senses.definition: a senior manager who makes important decisions in a company
senses.definitionCN: 在公司中做出重要决策的高级管理者
senses.example: The executive approved the new budget.
senses.exampleCN: 这位主管批准了新预算。
senses.why: The person at the top turns decisions into orders.
senses.whyCN: 顶层的人把决定变成指令。

senses.title: Administrative
senses.definition: connected with carrying out decisions and managing an organization
senses.definitionCN: 与执行决定和管理组织有关的
senses.example: The committee has executive power over spending.
senses.exampleCN: 该委员会在开支上拥有行政权。
senses.why: This branch of power is the one that acts.
senses.whyCN: 这一权力分支负责实际采取行动。

senses.title: High grade
senses.definition: designed for senior staff or wealthy customers
senses.definitionCN: 为高级职员或富裕顾客设计的
senses.example: They booked an executive suite on the top floor.
senses.exampleCN: 他们预订了顶层的行政套房。
senses.why: Even rooms borrow the status of the top floor.
senses.whyCN: 连房间也借用了顶层的身份感。

intro.en: Executive comes from Latin exsequi, to carry out.
intro.cn: executive 源自拉丁语 exsequi，意为执行到底。

items.en: Sequi means to follow.
items.cn: sequi 意为跟随。

items.en: Exsequi means to follow a task through.
items.cn: exsequi 意为把任务贯彻到底。

items.en: Executivus marks the power to carry out.
items.cn: executivus 标记付诸执行的权力。

items.en: French executif names the branch that acts.
items.cn: 法语 executif 指负责行动的那一支。

items.en: English executive extends to senior managers and luxury goods.
items.cn: 英语 executive 扩展到高级管理者与高档用品。

note.en: An executive decides and acts; a manager runs daily work.
note.cn: executive 决策并推动行动，manager 则负责日常运转。

entries.definition: the act of carrying out
entries.definitionCN: 执行；处决

entries.definition: a person who carries out a will
entries.definitionCN: 遗嘱执行人

entries.definition: to carry out
entries.definitionCN: 执行；实施

entries.definition: a person who runs daily work
entries.definitionCN: 经理；管理者

entries.definition: a person who manages an organization
entries.definitionCN: 管理者；行政人员

entries.definition: a member of a company board
entries.definitionCN: 董事；主管

normalIntro.en: An executive sits where decisions become action.
normalIntro.cn: executive 坐在决定变成行动的位置上。

normal.en: The chief executive sets the direction.
normal.cn: 首席执行官定下方向。

normal.en: Executive power belongs to the cabinet.
normal.cn: 行政权属于内阁。

normal.en: An executive director sits on the board.
normal.cn: 执行董事坐在董事会里。

normal.en: The executive suite has its own lounge.
normal.cn: 行政套房有自己的休息厅。

normal.en: Senior executives met to discuss the merger.
normal.cn: 高级主管们开会讨论合并。

abstract.en: Picture a corner office with the final say.
abstract.cn: 想象一间拥有最终决定权的拐角办公室。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand that signs and the plan moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手签下名字，计划就动起来。

abstract.en: Think of the top floor where decisions are made.
abstract.cn: 想象顶层那个做决定的楼层。

examples.en: The executive team meets every Monday.
examples.cn: 高管团队每周一开会。

examples.en: She became an executive at a young age.
examples.cn: 她年纪轻轻就成了高管。

examples.en: They stayed in an executive suite for the conference.
examples.cn: 他们为参加会议住进了行政套房。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「execut（执行）＋ ive」——负责拍板并推动执行的人就是主管；属于决策层的，就是行政的、高档的。

root: 拉丁语 exsequi（执行到底）→ executivus（有执行权的）→ executive，核心义「把决定付诸行动的人与层级」。

sensesIntro.en: Executive means a senior manager, the branch that carries out decisions, or goods made for top staff.
sensesIntro.cn: executive 意为高级管理者、负责执行的权力分支，或为高层服务的高档用品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corner office with the final say.
core.cn: 核心意象：拥有最终决定权的拐角办公室。

branches.en: The person who decides is the main sense.
branches.cn: 做决定的人是主要义项。

branches.en: The adjective marks the acting branch.
branches.cn: 形容词义标记负责行动的分支。

branches.en: The luxury sense serves top staff.
branches.cn: 高档义项服务于高层职员。

branches.en: Person and power both come from carrying out.
branches.cn: 人与权力都来自贯彻执行。

branches.en: Both point to the highest level.
branches.cn: 两者都指向最高层级。

intro.en: Executive combines ex-, out, with Latin sequi, to follow.
intro.cn: executive 由 ex-（出）与拉丁语 sequi（跟随）组成。

latinIntro.en: Executivus comes from exsequi and passes into French and English.
latinIntro.cn: executivus 来自 exsequi，再传入法语与英语。

items.exampleCN: executivus 加上了形容词词尾。
executor 加上了表示人的词尾。

definition_zh: 运输；运送；交通系统；运输工具
definition_en: the act of transporting people or goods, or the systems used for it
core_image: 整座城市的公交地图：把人和货送往四面八方的网
scene: 城市规划会议上，委员们讨论着地铁线路的延伸方案： On his first day the mayor announced that the whole city transportation system would be upgraded within three years.
sceneCN: 这里 transportation 是名词「交通系统」（第 2 个义项：承担运输的体系）；句意是市长宣布升级全市交通系统。

derivatives.zh: transportation 的动词根「运输」，同源词
由 transport 加 -er 构成，义为「运输者；运输车」
由 transport 加 -able 构成，义为「可运输的」

senses.title: The act or business of transporting goods and people
senses.definition: the business or act of carrying people or goods from place to place
senses.definitionCN: 把人或货物从一处运往另一处的事业或行为
senses.example: The cost of transportation rose sharply this winter.
senses.exampleCN: 今年冬天运输成本大幅上涨。
senses.why: The core image is the Latin act of carrying across, turned into a business.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是拉丁语「搬运过界」的动作被变成了一门生意。

senses.title: The systems and vehicles used for moving people
senses.definition: the systems, vehicles, and roads used for moving people and goods
senses.definitionCN: 运送人与货物所用的体系、车辆与道路
senses.example: Beijing has one of the largest transportation networks in the world.
senses.exampleCN: 北京拥有世界上规模最大的交通网络之一。
senses.why: One act of carrying grew into a whole network of buses, rails, and roads.
senses.whyCN: 一次搬运行为长成了公交、铁轨与道路组成的整张网。

senses.title: The fare or means by which one travels
senses.definition: vehicles used for travel, or money paid for the journey
senses.definitionCN: 出行所用的车辆，或出行所付的费用
senses.example: How will you cover transportation to the airport?
senses.exampleCN: 你打算怎么解决去机场的交通？
senses.why: In American English the network can also mean the ride itself.
senses.whyCN: 美式英语里这张网也能指「乘坐」本身。

intro.en: Transportation is transport plus the Latin noun suffix -ation, a making of the act into a name. Both verb and noun descend from Latin transportare, to carry across.
intro.cn: transportation 是 transport 加拉丁语名词后缀 -ation，把动作变成名称。动词与名词都源自拉丁语 transportare「搬运过去」。

items.en: portare meant to carry; trans- meant across.
items.cn: 拉丁语 portare 意为「搬运」，trans- 表示「跨越」。

items.en: transportare meant to carry across.
items.cn: 拉丁语 transportare 意为「搬运过去」。

items.en: Transport entered English for carrying goods and persons.
items.cn: transport 进入英语，指运送货物与人。

items.en: Transportation was formed as the action noun.
items.cn: transportation 作为动作名词被构造出来。

items.en: American English uses it for systems and vehicles; British English prefers transport.
items.cn: 美式英语用它指系统与工具，英式英语多用 transport。

note.en: Words that look or sound close to transportation, and words in the systems field.
note.cn: 与 transportation 形近音近的词，以及同属交通体系义场的词。

entries.definition: the verb root and the British noun
entries.definitionCN: 运输（动词；英式名词），transportation 的词根

entries.definition: a vehicle that transports
entries.definitionCN: 运输车，transport 加 -er 的派生

entries.definition: a complete change of form
entries.definitionCN: 变形，与 transportation 同以 trans- 开头但词根不同

entries.definition: the movement of people or goods
entries.definitionCN: 通行；运输过程，强调移动本身

entries.definition: the flow of vehicles
entries.definitionCN: 交通；车流，强调道路流量

entries.definition: the management of moving goods
entries.definitionCN: 物流，强调组织管理

entries.definition: the carrying of goods; old word for vehicle
entries.definitionCN: 货运；四轮马车（旧），旧式说法

normalIntro.en: Transportation is transport wearing the long -ation robe.
normalIntro.cn: transportation 就是披上 -ation 长袍的 transport。

normal.en: transport + ation = the noun of the system
normal.cn: transport 加 -ation＝系统的名词形式

normal.en: American: transportation, British: transport
normal.cn: 美式说 transportation，英式说 transport

normal.en: collocation: public transportation
normal.cn: 常用搭配 public transportation（公共交通）

normal.en: department of transportation in the US
normal.cn: 美国的交通部门用此词命名

normal.en: means of transportation = how you travel
normal.cn: means of transportation＝出行方式

abstract.en: A city map glowing with bus and metro lines
abstract.cn: 亮着公交与地铁线路的城市地图

abstract.en: A thousand trucks rolling out of a port at dawn
abstract.cn: 黎明时千辆卡车驶出港口

abstract.en: Coins dropped into a fare box before boarding
abstract.cn: 上车前把硬币投进投币箱

examples.en: The city invested heavily in public transportation.
examples.cn: 该市在公共交通上投入巨大。

examples.en: Transportation of fresh food needs cold chains.
examples.cn: 生鲜运输需要冷链。

examples.en: Her job is transportation planning for the county.
examples.cn: 她的工作是给全县做交通规划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踹死破太醒」——满城车流像被踹破的轮胎声太吵醒人：trans（过）+ port（搬）+ ation（大名词袍）→ transportation。

root: 拉丁语 trans-（跨越）+ portare（搬运）→ transportare；英语加 -ation 构成动作名词：运输这门事业与这张网。

sensesIntro.en: The act of carrying became a business, a network, and finally the ride itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 「搬运」的行为长成生意、长成网络，最终也指乘坐本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the whole network carrying a city day by day
core.cn: 核心意象：日复一日托起整座城市的交通网

branches.en: the business of moving goods and people
branches.cn: 运送人与货物的行业

branches.en: buses, rails, and roads as one system
branches.cn: 公交、铁轨与道路组成的整体

branches.en: the ride and the fare paid for it
branches.cn: 乘坐本身与所付车费

branches.en: from one carried load to a whole city network
branches.cn: 从一件被搬运的货物到整座城市的网络

branches.en: the network is used by buying a ride
branches.cn: 买一次乘坐，就接入整张网

intro.en: Transportation adds the Latin -ation to transport; the portare family carries the meaning.
intro.cn: transportation 在 transport 上加拉丁后缀 -ation；意义由 portare 词族承担。

latinIntro.en: Latin portare also gave portable, porter, export, and import.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 portare 还派生了 portable、porter、export 与 import。

items.meaning: to carry across; the British noun

definition_en: a plan for achieving something, or a secret and dishonest plot
core_image: 几个人在会议室角落低声交谈，桌上摊着一张利益地图
scene: 几个同事在暗地里密谋夺权。 A few colleagues schemed to take over the department.
sceneCN: 这里 scheme 是「密谋；策划」（第 3 个义项）；句意：几个同事密谋接管这个部门。

derivatives.zh: 阴谋家；计划者
诡计多端的
示意的；图解的
示意地

senses.title: Organized plan
senses.definition: an official or organized plan for achieving something
senses.definitionCN: 为实现某事而制定的正式或有组织的计划
senses.example: The city launched a new recycling scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市启动了一项新的回收计划。
senses.why: The core sense is an arranged outline of action.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是安排好的行动纲要。

senses.title: Secret plot
senses.definition: a secret plan to gain an advantage over others
senses.definitionCN: 为取得对他人优势而制定的秘密计划
senses.example: The scheme was discovered before it began.
senses.exampleCN: 这个阴谋在开始前就被发现了。
senses.why: A private plan turns dark when it harms others.
senses.whyCN: 当计划伤害他人时，私下的计划就变得阴暗。

senses.title: Plot secretly
senses.definition: to make secret plans, often to harm others
senses.definitionCN: 制定秘密计划，常指损害他人
senses.example: They schemed to win the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 他们密谋赢得合同。
senses.why: The noun becomes the act of plotting.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为密谋的动作。

senses.title: System or arrangement
senses.definition: an organized system such as a pension or benefit arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 如养老金或福利安排的有组织体系
senses.example: The pension scheme covers all staff.
senses.exampleCN: 养老金计划覆盖所有员工。
senses.why: A plan for many people becomes an institution.
senses.whyCN: 为许多人制定的计划变成一种制度。

intro.en: Scheme comes from Greek schema, a form or figure, through Latin schema.
intro.cn: scheme 经拉丁语 schema 源自希腊语 schema（形状、图形）。

items.en: Schema meant form, shape, or figure.
items.cn: schema 意为形式、形状或图形。

items.en: Schema meant a figure or a plan.
items.cn: schema 意为图形或计划。

items.en: Scheme entered English as a diagram or outline.
items.cn: scheme 以图表或纲要之义进入英语。

items.en: Scheme gained the sense of a secret plot.
items.cn: scheme 获得阴谋的含义。

items.en: Scheme covers official programmes and private plots.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scheme 兼指官方方案与私下阴谋。

note.en: Scheme is compared with similar spellings and with words for plans and plots.
note.cn: 把 scheme 与形近词以及表示计划和阴谋的词作比较。

entries.definition: an outline or model
entries.definitionCN: 纲要；图式

entries.definition: a timetable
entries.definitionCN: 时间表

entries.definition: a place or unit of action
entries.definitionCN: 场景；现场

entries.definition: an intended course of action
entries.definitionCN: 计划

entries.definition: a secret plan
entries.definitionCN: 阴谋

entries.definition: a plan or purpose
entries.definitionCN: 设计；意图

normalIntro.en: Scheme began as a shape and became a plan drawn to that shape.
normalIntro.cn: scheme 最初指形状，后来指按那个形状画出的计划。

normal.en: A scheme is a plan with a clear outline.
normal.cn: 方案就是有清晰轮廓的计划。

normal.en: A pension scheme is an official plan.
normal.cn: pension scheme 是官方计划。

normal.en: A secret scheme is a plot.
normal.cn: 秘密的方案就是阴谋。

normal.en: To scheme against someone is to plot quietly.
normal.cn: scheme against someone 就是暗中算计某人。

normal.en: Schematic drawings show a plan in simple lines.
normal.cn: schematic 图用简单线条表示方案。

abstract.en: Every scheme is a shape imposed on the future.
abstract.cn: 每个方案都是强加给未来的一种形状。

abstract.en: A plan for everyone and a plot by a few share one word.
abstract.cn: 为众人的计划与少数人的阴谋共用一个词。

abstract.en: Schemes reveal what people want before they say it.
abstract.cn: 计谋在人开口之前就暴露了他们想要什么。

examples.en: The government introduced a training scheme.
examples.cn: 政府推出了一项培训方案。

examples.en: Two managers schemed to remove the director.
examples.cn: 两名经理密谋撤掉主管。

examples.en: Their scheme collapsed when the emails were leaked.
examples.cn: 邮件泄露后，他们的阴谋破产了。

dict_mnemonic.text: scheme 与 schema 同源，本义是「形状、图式」；把未来画成图就是方案，偷偷画的就是阴谋。

root: 源自希腊语 schema（形状、图式），经拉丁语 schema 入英语，核心义「为行动画出的轮廓」。

sensesIntro.en: Scheme means an official plan, a secret plot, to plot, or an organized system.

core.en: An outline drawn for future action.
core.cn: 为未来行动画出的轮廓。

branches.en: A public plan for achieving something.
branches.cn: 为实现某事而制定的公开计划。

branches.en: A hidden plan that harms others.
branches.cn: 损害他人的秘密计划。

branches.en: The act of making secret plans.
branches.cn: 制定秘密计划的动作。

branches.en: A plan that becomes a system for many people.
branches.cn: 成为许多人制度的计划。

branches.en: Public and secret plans share the same outline.
branches.cn: 公开计划与秘密计划共享同一轮廓。

intro.en: Scheme has a family of planners, plotters, and diagrams.
intro.cn: scheme 有规划者、阴谋者与图表构成的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin schema, a form, is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 schema（形状）是直接来源。

items.structure: English plural noun and third person form
